points: Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: They lifted up their voice and wept again; Orpah kissed her mother in law and went back, but Ruth clave unto her.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Ruth clave to Naomi: thy people shall be my people and thy God my God; she is the picture of the ten men who will take hold of the skirt of a Jew and say, we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Ruth was determined: Intreat me not to leave thee; whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God; where thou diest, will I die. She was saying, do not put me away; Orpah may have gone back, but I am going to cleave unto you.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter in law with her, and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Ruth asked Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace; and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: She answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.

On the skirt: Zondervan's Compact Bible Dictionary, page 137, explains that the basic garments of the men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle, and the cloak, with the headdress and the shoes or sandals; the word skirt in the Bible usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, and carries meanings such as extremity, as in Ruth 3:9. Asking Boaz to spread his skirt over her was asking the near kinsman to take her under his covering.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

points: Boaz was not the closest kinsman, so he asked the nearer one first: if you redeem it, you must also take Ruth and raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive.

What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.
Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and purchased Ruth to be his wife to raise up the name of the dead, that it be not cut off from among his brethren.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Boaz said unto the elders and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi; moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place.
Boaz went in unto her and the Lord gave her conception; that is what happens when a man goes in unto a woman, and by the Christian reading the Lord would have lain with Ruth.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.
Generation goes back to genes and genealogy: Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar, Phares begat Esrom, down to Naasson, Salmon, Booz of Rachab, Obed of Ruth, Jesse and David the king.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Boaz begat Obed of Ruth is where levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question asked.
